scope: The standing Chaleemongkolasana and Maleeratanabanlang exteriors at Sanam Chandra Palace and their physically attached upper-floor covered crossing. Includes the north château façade and spired corner towers, red-tile roofs, timber Thai-Western residence and roofed bridge. The separately placed dog monument, shrine and northern halls have independent scopes.
state: named footprints, public-domain château reference and original terrain frozen

primaryWrittenSources.author: Sunon Palakavong Na Ayudhya
primaryWrittenSources.facts: The two-storey concrete and red-tiled château has a pointed arch and timber detailing. The attached two-storey red teak residence uses rounded arches, a red tile hipped roof and a timber corridor bridge that meets both upper floors over the moat.

primaryWrittenSources.author: Sanamchandra Palace Library, Silpakorn University
primaryWrittenSources.facts: Both named residences survive within the palace grounds and were restored.

next: Freeze the native terrain field and build the mapped connected pair, starting with the pale yellow north château façade, tower roofs and half-timber bay.
limits: North château modeling follows the exact Ananda public-domain original. Rear opening spacing, roof heights, turret cross sections and trim motifs are medium-fi estimates.

Maleeratanabanlang uses the named mapped perimeter and the published descriptions of two red teak storeys, rounded arches and timber corridor. Its facade rhythm, hip configuration, bridge glazing and supporting piers are estimated.

The 256 m public source terrain is unchanged. The grade around the moat and elevations of its banks are approximate. The main entrance and companion threshold are independently grounded, and a modest continuous bridge pitch keeps the covered upper-floor passage connected.
Covers the two connected residences and covered crossing. The dog monument, other halls, landscaping and the campus are separate site scopes.
